topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: Matrices represent transformations of coordinate systems.
Basis vectors define the transformed space.
Square matrices map space to itself.
animations: Create unit vectors i-hat and j-hat with light-blue color #ADD8E6.
Show 2D grid plane scaling based on basis vectors using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg].
Transform i-hat and j-hat vectors to new positions.
Label i-hat as [1,0] and j-hat as [0,1] in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight span of vectors as filled area in light-grey #D3D3D3.

sections.title: The 'Expansion' Scenario: Embedding 2D into 3D
animations: Place unit vectors i-hat and j-hat on the plane.
Show grid transforming to cover 3D space.

sections.title: The 'Projection' Scenario: Compressing 3D into 2D
animations: Show 3D [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] grid and vectors in light-purple #E6E6FA.
Map 3D points down to a 2D plane.

sections.title: Visualizing the Rank: Why Information is Lost
lecture_lines: Rank is the dimensionality of output.
animations: Visualize a matrix transformation causing collapse using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/projector.svg].

Explain how multiple inputs map to same output using the refraction logic of a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg].
